text:
maya: Proposal: decompose the request-router monolith into 4 smaller services: ingest, router-core, policy-evaluator, response-cache. goal: clear ownership + remove global state. looking for feedback on migration approach and handoff timeline.

josh: 👍 overall makes sense. main concern: how do we keep rollout low-risk for hosted customers?

anika: +1 on split. we should keep a compatibility shim so existing clients see no contract change. also need per-tenant routing metadata persistence plan.

ryan: infra note: we should be able to run all four as a single `rr-composed` helm chart for first pass (same nodes) and then split namespaces later. gives us easier rollback.

maya: here's a rough migration plan: 1) extract ingest (stateless) + shim that forwards to legacy router; 2) extract router-core behind feature-flag; 3) move policy evaluation out of hot path to policy-evaluator with sidecar cache; 4) enable response-cache gradually by route. canary per-customer at each step.

josh: sounds good. DB question: where does routing metadata live? single table in global DB today. moving to service-owned store is messy. suggestion: write-proxy pattern: all writes go to new service store, reads fallback to legacy until cutover.

anika: agree on write-proxy. also add a migration job that backfills existing rows into the new store, run in batches. avoid per-request dual writes for >2 weeks.

ryan: infra-bot: what infra changes are blockers?

infra-bot: room:deploy-scheduler created for rr-decompose. required: 2 new nodepools (cpu-ssd for policy-evaluator, gpu-free for response-cache tests), RBAC entries for router-core team, additional SLO dashboards.

maya: API shim example (for compatibility):
```
POST /v1/requests -> ingest-service (validate, auth)
ingest-service -> legacy-router (via X-Forwarded-For header)
// once router-core is ready, ingest-service -> router-core with same header
```

josh: important: maintain idempotency keys at ingest layer. legacy router assumes per-request idempotency from headers. document this in the shim.

anika: ownership: propose these owners - ingest: platform team (maya lead), router-core: serving team (josh lead), policy-evaluator: security/ops (anika lead), response-cache: performance (ryan lead).

ryan: agreed, but add cross-team SLOs and escalation path. we had past incidents where split ownership led to blame-shifting.

maya: yes. I'll draft an SLO matrix and a small runbook for each service. suggestion: shared pager for first 4 weeks after cutover.

josh: rollout strategy detail: feature-flag with percent-based rollout + customer whitelist. example flags: `rr_ingest_v2`, `rr_core_v1`, `policy_sidecar_v1`, `response_cache_beta`.

anika: for observability: instrument per-request trace id propagation, plus route-level latency percentiles. create alert: router-core 95th > 300ms for 5m.

ryan: data plane migration: ensure we can replay legacy logs into new services if we need to rehydrate caches. keep a read-only replica for 2 months.

maya: tech debt paydown items to bundle with this work: - remove global config singletons - move feature flags into config-store - extract metrics reporting into lib (no side effects) - tidy up global error types into a small contract file

josh: timeline proposal: 6 sprints (12 weeks) for extract+canary of ingest+router-core, add 4 weeks for policy-evaluator + cache stabilization. total ~4 months. ok?

anika: +1 but call out weekends for DB migration jobs. also reserve 2 days for rollback drills per major cutover.

ryan: we need a small test harness that can replay real traffic samples (anonymized). who owns that? platform team?

maya: platform will own harness and provide traffic buckets. will sync with data-privacy for sample extraction.

josh: can we get a small compatibility e2e job in CI that runs against composed chart? catches contract drift early.

maya: yes, I'll add e2e gate that verifies request/response contract across shim.

anika: decision checkpoints: 1) ingest extraction + shim approved, 2) router-core API spec signed off, 3) DB write-proxy tested, 4) policy sidecar performance review. we should make them formal RFC follow-ups.

maya: I'll draft follow-up RFC with the checkpoints and owners. action items: @josh to draft router-core API by next Tue, @ryan to list infra reqs this week, @anika to write DB migration plan, @maya to write SLOs + RFC.

josh: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:

anika: thanks — will include rollback playbook snippets in migration doc. :eyes:

maya: closing thread for now, moving RFC to google drive and tagging this convo. will ping when draft ready.
